scope: Proposition 3.9 (Alignment of model orbits) of the manuscript “Eventual categoricity for abstract elementary classes” (preprints/Eventual-Categoricity-for-Abstract-Elementary-Classes-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 240 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dcb7401285f5ac78), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 19. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix the record set and orbit naming at an infinite length θ. Let a < µ be categoricity cardinals with a ≥ max(ℓ, θ+). Suppose the following data have one common profile: 1. a presentation E(H(β)) of Cµ, where β is additively indecomposable, |β| = µ, and cf(β) > a; 2. presentations E(H(δ)) of Ca for a cofinal subset of a+ of additively indecomposable ordinals δ of size a and cofinality greater than θ. Then in any copy N of Cµ, every subset of size at most a is contained in A ≤K N of size a such that the orbit name of every θ-tuple in A, computed as a tuple of Ca, is the same as its name computed in N.
